I added `migrations/003_exports_status_default.sql`. I haven't run it, and the project has no tests or migration runner I could use to check it.

The migration does three things:
1. It backfills existing rows where `status` is NULL to `'queued'`.
2. It sets the column default to `'queued'`.
3. It sets the column to `NOT NULL`.

I made it a new migration because `001_init.sql` has probably already been applied. Editing it wouldn't change existing databases. The backfill has to run before `SET NOT NULL`, or that step would fail on the NULL rows already in the table.

Backfilling every NULL row to `'queued'` assumes those jobs haven't started. If some of them have actually run, you may want to set their status by hand before applying the migration.
